content: Do not take lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it can harm the developing fetus. Lisinopril belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, which work by reducing certain chemicals that constrict blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill, which helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt through urine. This medication is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to any of its components, including lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, or other related medications such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, or sulfa drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with this medication. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are undergoing dialysis, desensitization therapy, or if you have a history of allergies, asthma, diabetes, gout, high cholesterol, collagen vascular diseases (e.g., lupus or scleroderma), heart failure, reduced urination, stroke, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, or angioedema (a condition causing swelling and difficulty breathing or swallowing). Additionally, let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant, are pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can exacerbate the side effects of this medication. This medication may also cause dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when standing up quickly. To minimize this effect, rise slowly from a lying or seated position. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor recommends a low-sodium diet or an exercise program, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience dizziness, headache, cough, fatigue, tingling or burning sensations in the hands or feet, reduced sexual ability, or heartburn. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, or extremities; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; stomach pain; nausea; vomiting; fever; chills; muscle pain or weakness; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dry mouth; excessive thirst; confusion; seizures; reduced urination; fainting; chest pain; irregular heartbeat; pain in the big toe; tingling in the limbs; loss of muscle tone; cold or gray skin; or extreme fatigue. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness, fainting, blurred vision, dry mouth, thirst, weakness, drowsiness, restlessness, confusion, seizures, muscle cramps, reduced urination, nausea, vomiting, or a rapid or irregular heartbeat. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking this medication. Inform laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refills. This medication is sold under the brand names Prinzide® and Zestoretic®.
